frequency_question: What is the base rate frequency of formal federal recognition revocations or forced terminations among major national accrediting bodies over a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal agency action by the U.S. Department of Education (or equivalent federal bodies) seeking to strip an established institutional or programmatic accreditor of its federal recognition status. Excludes routine renewals, voluntary relinquishments, or minor compliance notices without formal revocation proceedings.
window: 28-month forward-looking observation window (corresponding to the period up to 31 December 2026)

cases.name: American Bar Association (prior departmental compliance reviews and limitation/probation threats)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) - First Revocation Action
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) - Second Final Termination
American Board of Funeral Service Education (prolonged compliance tracking without revocation)

provenance_note: claims 15 cases from only 4 named (3.8x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 named explicitly as major regulatory friction points; estimated ~15 total intensive agency compliance challenge cycles resulting in formal termination proceedings or close threats over 25 years.
known_gaps: Specialized professional school accreditors (like law) face different statutory protections and institutional inertia compared to programmatic for-profit career college accreditors like ACICS.
skeleton: Formal recognition review cycles for major national/professional accreditors over the past three decades, divided into cycles of heightened federal scrutiny versus standard renewals.
multiplier: 2 major executed revocations out of approximately 15 distinct high-scrutiny compliance actions against recognized accreditors since 2000.
validity_reason: Regulatory frameworks governing federal recognition of accreditors remain stable across multi-year administrative cycles, but shift with major statutory revisions to the Higher Education Act.
